facts.value: There are 4 different Business English courses (A-B-C-D) as part of the elective module courses in Business English.
All elective module courses have the same difficulty level (target level C1.1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages).
Successful completion of a qualifying test at CEFR level B2.2, held at the beginning of each semester if no Bachelor's elective module course in Business English has been successfully completed.
Two-stage application process with different deadlines. You must participate in both stages and pass the online qualifying test.
Registration period: September 21, 2026 – October 5, 2026 via QIS.
Exam registration and deregistration period: October 8, 2026 – October 21, 2026 via QIS.

Exceptions: Students with a Cambridge Certificate C1, a score of at least 100 points in the TOEFL test or a score of at least 7.5 in the IELTS test must upload this language proof in PDF format during the online qualifying test.
Elective Module Course A: Current Global Economic Affairs
Monetary and financial policy, energy policy, global trade, migration and labor markets.
Joanne Glen, Guojun Wong, Barry Hawthorne.
Group 1: Mon. 14:00 – 16:00, starts October 12, 2026. Group 2: Tue. 12:00 – 14:00, starts October 13, 2026. Group 3: Thu. 10:00 – 12:00, starts October 15, 2026.
Elective Module Course B: Marketing
Marketing mix, behavioral economics and consumer behavior, digital marketing, gender, ethnicity and marketing, artificial intelligence, sustainability and ethical marketing, political marketing.
Caroline Pung.
Wed. 14:00 – 16:00, starts October 14, 2026.
Elective Module Course C: The Entrepreneur
The entrepreneur and entrepreneurship, market research and feasibility analysis, strategy and pricing, marketing and branding, financial projections and financing.
Barry Hawthorne.
Tue. 10:00 – 12:00, starts October 13, 2026.
Elective Module Course D: Banking & Financial Topics

Alternative finance: crowdfunding / shadow banking / complementary currencies, fintech: cryptocurrencies / cashless societies / fintech startups, ethical/social banking: Islamic banking / microfinance / climate & capitalism, topics of current interest: stock market crisis / zombie companies / trade wars.
Caroline Pung.
Tue. 16:00 – 18:00, starts October 13, 2026.
All participants receive 6 credit points for the successful completion of a Business English elective module course: English for Economists.
An internal C1.1 certificate is issued for the successfully completed course.
